sentences: A single face fills a sheet of paper not much bigger than two open hands.
There are no visible ears, no neck, no body: only a pair of eyes staring straight ahead and a beard that flares out like a flame.
Joseon portraits usually showed sitters at a slight angle in formal official robes, so a bare, head-on self-portrait like this was radical.
For years some scholars thought it was unfinished.
Then in 2006 the National Museum of Korea examined it with infrared and X-ray imaging and found that the ears, the collar and the folds of a robe had once been painted.
Nearly three hundred years of fading had simply erased the lighter lines, leaving the face alone.
